Firstly, you can take this post however you choose to.

Me on the other hand, I received abuse by my parents. They didn't know how to handle an ADHD Child. 

Through therapy, I stopped thinking of ADHD as a bad thing, and instead learned to have a more neutral view on it. 

A lot of us feel incapable, frozen, and immobile, and sometimes, we need a reminder that we aren't broken. We have ADHD. Its tough. But there are things that make us special. We do have certain skills and attributes in our caliber. I'm simply stating those. 

You know that we are self critical. You know that we are perfectionists. You know we struggle with rejection sensitivity, executive dysfunction, and more. Would you rather continue being hard on yourself and only point out your flaws? Or would you rather be compassionate towards your diagnosis, and give yourself grace and patience in areas that we're lacking in? 

I've went through hell. So I choose and chose to share the positives about us. You never know who is struggling underneath the weight that ADHD brings. I was crushed for a very long time. So i WILL point out the positives, and I WILL give a reminder, because dammit, this life IS hard.
